title: The canonical constant coefficient comparison is invertible
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes and $A$ any commutative ring. Use the constant coefficient ring sheaves $A_Y,A_X$ and the canonical map $c_A^f$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Then $c_A^f:f^{-1}A_Y\to A_X$ is an isomorphism of commutative ring sheaves. No finiteness, nonemptiness, or invertibility assumption is required.

proof.text: The object (Y,id_Y) is terminal in the pro-etale site: its unique incoming map is the structure morphism. The base-change functor preserves this terminal object by finite-limit preservation in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. The constant-sheaf functor is left adjoint to evaluation at either terminal object. Compose the constant-sheaf adjunction on Y with the inverse-image adjunction. Evaluation after direct image equals evaluation at the base-changed terminal object. Uniqueness of left adjoints therefore supplies an isomorphism f^{-1}A_Y≅A_X. This works in commutative rings with the stipulated lifted coefficient universe.

The existing constantComparison_isIso proof checks that the adjoint-uniqueness isomorphism is the canonical coefficient map. Apply the inverse-image Hom equivalence, then the constant-sheaf Hom equivalence. The constant-section unit formula and sheafification Hom equivalence identify the map at the terminal object. Thus the hom of the adjoint-uniqueness isomorphism equals the specified coefficient map, which is therefore invertible. This existing proof is reused unchanged; only its visibility is public.
